description: Existing Dictionary wording retained during source-data recovery on 2026-10-24. These entries override historical source definitions and listening additions.

concepts.MC-0001: An African American style that developed from spirituals, work songs and field hollers. It is commonly in 4/4 and often follows a 12-bar chord pattern. Characteristic features include use of a blues scale, call and response, repeated riffs and improvisation.
concepts.MC-0086: The interval between one note and the next higher or lower note with the same letter name, such as C to the next C. The two notes sound closely related, although one is higher or lower.
concepts.MC-0296: The principal musical theme on which a work or section is based. The term is used especially for the main theme of a fugue and for the first and second subjects in sonata form.
